I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County, that is the most practical way for me to use the land for the whole year, and at my age I would choose a system that is familiar, easy to arrange with local machines, and reliable in both grain output and selling. I do not want to take on a risky cash crop that needs closer management, more labor, or more market guessing. Wheat and maize fit my experience, fit the local climate on the North China Plain, and spread the work across the year in a way I can still handle.

For seed, I will use improved seed rather than traditional saved seed. I want steadier emergence, better disease tolerance, and more stable yield, but I do not want to pay for a crop system that is too complicated. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to arrange and lighter than deep ploughing every season. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate rate: enough to support yield, but not so much that I waste money or push the crop too hard. Wheat will get more careful water management because spring moisture matters a lot for tillering, jointing, and grain filling. Maize will get fewer irrigations, mainly depending on rain plus one or two key irrigations if needed. I will keep pesticide sprays limited and only use the number I think is necessary to protect the crop, because I want to control cost and avoid unnecessary work.
